name: Ga'anda
sweep_summary: Ga'anda (gaan1243) is not in the catalog. The sweep list had one item, Newman 1977 'Y-prosody as a morphological process in Ga'anda'. The whole 1977 Leiden colloquium volume is open access at hdl.handle.net/1887/468 (Leiden University repository); curl with a default UA is blocked by Leiden's protection page but a Chrome UA downloads the 22.8 MB image-only PDF, with. Pages 121-130 (PDF 133-142) were scanned at 250 dpi. The paper is a false positive for word stress: 'Y-prosody' is Firthian prosodic-analysis terminology for a morphologically conditioned palatalization feature (central vowels fronted, s > sh, final velar nasal > y) marking noun modified stems and 2nd/3rd-sg verb forms. Its only suprasegmental statement is footnote 5 (p. 121): 'Ga'anda has a three-tone system plus downstep (see R. Newman 1971b)'; stress/accent never occur in the text. No first-hand word-stress statement for Ga'anda was found. Remaining leads: Newman 1971b 'Downstep in Ga'anda' (JAL 10, tone; no online record found via OpenAlex/Crossref) and the 1971 UCLA dissertation (HathiTrust search-only; the only full grammar, medium priority for any phonology-chapter remark on stress).org, OpenAlex, Crossref and Wikipedia (the Wikipedia Ga'anda page has no phonology section).

earlier_scan.source_named: Newman, Roxana Ma 1971. A Case Grammar of Ga'anda. UCLA PhD dissertation (cited on Wikipedia Ga'anda page; no online copy found)

sources.citation: Newman, Roxana Ma (1977). Y-prosody as a morphological process in Ga'anda. In Paul Newman & Roxana Ma Newman (eds.), Papers in Chadic Linguistics: papers from the Leiden Colloquium on the Chadic Language Family (Leiden, 15-17 September 1976), 121-130. Leiden: Afrika-Studiecentrum (Research reports 4).
sources.quote: SGa'anda has a three-tone system plus downstep (see R. Newman 1971b). Downstep occurs when a Hi tone is preceded by a non-segmental Mid or Lo tone (indicated by ' or ' written over a consonant, hyphen, or space). [fn. 5, p. 121] ... The overriding feature shared by these changes is palatality or "Y-coloration", functioning in the morphology as "Y-prosody". It is viewed as a prosodic feature because it applies to the entire noun stem, affecting all relevant segments within this domain. [p. 126] ... They involve primarily fronting of certain vowels and palatalization of certain consonants. [p. 121]
sources.locator: pp. 121 (opening paragraph and footnote 5), 126-127 (definition of Y-prosody), 130 (conclusion)
sources.note: Nothing. 'Prosody' here is Firthian: Y-prosody is a stem-wide palatalization feature (central vowels fronted, s > sh, stem-final velar nasal > y) that marks the modified stem of Y-class nouns and 2nd/3rd-sg-subject verb forms, and is morphologically not phonologically conditioned. The only suprasegmental statement in the paper is footnote 5: Ga'anda has a three-tone system plus downstep (citing R. Newman 1971b). The words stress/accent/prominence do not occur anywhere in the scanned paper (checked with fuzzy grep). The scanned of tone marks is unreliable but the prose is clean.
